category_title: Verbal students with HFA who struggle with environmental distractions and role ambiguity
minimal_context: The student is working in an OpenSim virtual environment to build a Japanese neighborhood.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start building the virtual Japanese neighborhood in OpenSim. Please place your first architectural item on the island.

STUDENT: I am very excited to start building. I will place the first item and refine its position and size now.

TUTOR: Great, go ahead and tell me what you are doing.

STUDENT: Yes, but I cannot understand you. What ’s that sound?

TUTOR: That is just the background ocean wind in the virtual environment. Please continue with the task.

STUDENT: I cannot understand you. There is a lot of noise!

options.A: Provide a reflective journal prompt about the design task that includes a set of metacognitive prompts ('My Analysis', 'My Motivation', 'My Problem', 'My Plan') and prompt sheets.
options.B: Draw some boundaries on the virtual island, label more of the architectural dimensions, and provide explicit explanations of the spatial relationships within the environment.
options.C: Explain via both text and verbal chat that the noise is the ocean wind blowing through the trees, then encourage the student to fly with the partner to an open space where the wind noise would be reduced.
options.D: Introduce new architectural design strategies in the virtual environment through modeling their use by thinking aloud during the activity.
